title: Both sides must make sense
text: You must make sure that both sides make sense.

title: LHS
text: For which values of $$x$$ is the left-hand side $$\frac{x}{x+1}$$ undefined?

subHints.title: LHS
subHints.text: $$\frac{x}{x+1}$$ is undefined when the denominator is zero: $$x+1=0$$. That is, it is undefined when $$x=-1$$.

title: RHS
text: For which values of $$x$$ is the right-hand side $$\frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{x}}$$ undefined?

subHints.title: RHS
subHints.text: $$\frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{x}}$$ is undefined when $$\frac{1}{x}$$ is undefined and when $$1+\frac{1}{x}=0$$. This happens when $$x=0$$ or when $$x=-1$$.

title: Conclusion
text:
An equation cannot be true at any value where either side is undefined. 
 - The left hand side is undefined for $$x=-1$$ 
 - The right hand side is undefined when $$x=0$$ and $$x=-1$$. 
 
 Ruling out every value that causes a problem on either side, we see that the equivalence fails when $$x=0$$ and $$x=-1$$.
